text: Kwadwo Baah-Wiredu (1952 – 24 September 2008) was a Ghanaian politician and a chartered accountant. He served as Member of Parliament for Asante Akim North Constituency from January 1997 until his death on 24 September 2008. He held ministerial positions under the Kufuor government from 2001, serving as Minister of Local Government and Rural Development (2001–2003) and Minister of Education, Youth and Sports (2003–2005), before becoming Minister for Finance and Economic Planning in 2005. In 2005, he became the first Finance Minister in Ghana's history to present the country's Budget Statement and Economic Policy to Parliament before the start of the fiscal year 2006, a practice that has since become standard for all Finance Ministers. Baah-Wiredu was born in Asante Akim Agogo. He began secondary education at Kumasi High School in 1967, obtained the GCE Ordinary Level Certificate in 1972, and completed his sixth form at Prempeh College, both in Kumasi. He enrolled at the University of Ghana in 1974, earning a B.Sc. in Administration (Accounting option), and later completed a four-year course with the Institute of Chartered Accountants, qualifying as a chartered accountant in 1985. He worked at Ghana Airways and the Volta River Authority, served as a senior consultant on computer systems and finance manager at Ananse Systems, and was a partner in Asante Wiredu and Associates, an accounting firm. He began his political career in 1997 as Member of Parliament for Asante Akim North following his victory in the 1996 Ghanaian General Election. He joined the New Patriotic Party in 1992 and was elected to the Second Parliament of the Fourth Republic in 1996, retaining his seat thereafter. In 2000, he won the general election for Asante Akim North, securing 32,341 votes out of 45,227 valid votes cast (72.3%), defeating Kofi Opoku Manu (11,852 votes, 26.5%), Kwabena Anafi (168 votes, 0.4%), James K. Baah (151 votes, 0.3%), Emmanuel K. Adade (130 votes, 0.3%), and Joseph B. Frimpong (75 votes, 0.2%). In 2004, he won again on the New Patriotic Party ticket, receiving 40,497 votes out of 53,098 valid votes cast (76.3%), defeating Atobrah Isaac (0.8%), Thomas Osei Bonsu Nkansah (21.6%), and Kwabena Anarfi (1.3%). His constituency was part of the 31 seats won by the New Patriotic Party in the Ashanti Region in 2000 and 36 seats in 2004, with the party winning a total of 99 seats (200 total) in 2000 and 128 seats (230 total) in 2004. Baah-Wiredu was married with six children. He died on 24 September 2008 in South Africa, where he had been receiving medical treatment for a short illness.
